;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Second Nagorno-Karabakh War]]
**A [[Russia]]n [[Mil Mi-24]] helicopter is [[2020 Russian Mil Mi-24 shootdown|shot down]] by the [[Azerbaijani Armed Forces]] over [[Armenia]], near the [[Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic]]. Russia says two crew members are killed. [[Azerbaijan]] apologizes, extends condolences, and offers to pay compensation. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-54874162 (BBC News)]
**[[Republic of Artsakh|Artsakh]] officials in [[Nagorno-Karabakh]] confirm the loss of [[Shusha]] to Azeri forces. Many civilians in Shusha have fled, and fighting is closing on the region's capital, [[Stepanakert]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/11/9/ethnic-armenians-confirm-loss-of-shusha-to-azeri-forces (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Prime Minister of Armenia|Armenian Prime Minister]] [[Nikol Pashinyan]] announces he has signed a deal with [[Azerbaijan]] and [[Russia]] to end the war by Tuesday morning. A [[Kremlin]] spokesman confirms the deal. Later, [[President of Azerbaijan|Azerbaijan's president]] [[Ilham Aliyev]] says a "trilateral agreement" has been signed. [[President of Russia]] [[Vladimir Putin]] says [[Russia]]n [[Peacekeeping|peacekeepers]] will be deployed. The agreement cedes several districts to Azerbaijan, including the [[Lachin District]]. The agreement will also establish a transport corridor through Armenia, linking Azerbaijan to [[Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic|Nakhchivan]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-armenia-azerbaijan/armenia-says-signs-deal-with-azerbaijan-and-russia-to-end-conflict-idUSKBN27P1FL (Reuters)]
**The peace deal is met with anger in Armenia as [[2020–2021 Armenian protests|thousands protest]] against it in the [[Capital city|capital]] [[Yerevan]] with some protesters storming the parliament building. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/nov/10/nagorno-karabakh-armenia-pm-signs-deal-to-end-war-with-azerbaijan-and-russia (''The Guardian'')]
**Hours after signing of the deal, [[Ararat Mirzoyan]], the [[President of the National Assembly of Armenia|president]] of [[Armenia]]'s [[National Assembly (Armenia)|National Assembly]], is pulled from his car and attacked by an angry mob of protesters. [https://www.interfax.ru/world/736343 (Interfax)]
*[[ISIL insurgency in Iraq (2017–present)|ISIL insurgency in Iraq]]
**Unidentified gunmen using [[grenade]]s and [[automatic weapon]]s attacked an army post in western [[Baghdad]], killing 11 people, including soldiers. Both the military and [[Iraqi Police|police]] have launched a manhunt for the gunmen. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/11/9/gunmen-kill-11-in-attack-on-iraqi-army-post-in-baghdad (Al Jazeera)]

;Business and economy
*The [[Dow Jones Industrial Average]] opens at an all-time record high – a 1,500-point surge in reaction to [[Pfizer]]'s results in testing its [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.foxbusiness.com/markets/us-stocks-november-9-2020 (Fox Business)]
*In the United States, a biannual [[Federal Reserve]] report mentions, for the first time, [[climate change]] as a risk for the stability of the [[financial system]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-fed-stability-climate/in-first-for-fed-u-s-central-bank-says-climate-poses-stability-risks-idUSKBN27P2T9 (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Albania]]
****[[Albania]] announces that it will impose a second nationwide [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] on November 11 in an attempt to curb the worsening spread of COVID-19. [https://albaniandailynews.com/news/albania-imposes-new-lockdown-as-covid-19-cases-soar (''Albanian Daily News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium]]
****[[Belgium]] surpasses 500,000 total confirmed cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.brusselstimes.com/news/belgium-all-news/139911/belgium-reaches-total-of-more-than-half-a-million-covid-19-cases-coronavirus-infections-hospital-admissions-intensive-care-icu-ventilator-deaths-sciensano/ (''The Brussels Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[Greece]] reports a record 41 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, raising its death toll to 825. [https://www.ekathimerini.com/258977/article/ekathimerini/news/authorities-report-a-record-breaking-41-covid-19-deaths (''Ekathimerini'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Prime Minister of Hungary|Prime Minister]] [[Viktor Orbán]] announces that a curfew will be implemented between 8:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m  local time and orders restaurants and bars to close. Meanwhile, the curfew also prohibits gatherings of more than ten people, reintroduces online learning for high schools and universities, and sports events will be held only behind closed doors. The measures, which last for an initial 30 days, will be voted on in the [[National Assembly (Hungary)|National Assembly]] tomorrow and come into force on November 11. [https://hungarytoday.hu/updating-govt-to-extend-curfew-from-8-pm-to-5-am-starting-from-wednesday/ (Hungary Today)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports 21,798 new infections in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record since they began, thus bringing the cumulative nationwide total to 1.79 million cases. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2020/11/09/russia-reports-over-21k-coronavirus-infections-in-latest-record-a71987 (''The Moscow Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[President of Ukraine|President]] [[Volodymyr Zelensky]] and two top government officials test positive for COVID-19. [https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-ukrainian-president-volodymyr-zelensky-tests-positive-for-covid-19/ (''The Globe and Mail'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports a record 10,463 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total since the [[pandemic]] began to 692,949 cases. [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/iran-reports-record-daily-coronavirus-cases-of-10463-6485059 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Hokkaido]] reports a record 200 new cases in the past 24 hours. [https://www.nippon.com/en/news/yjj2020110900481/ (Nippon.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] reports 108 new deaths in the past 24 hours, its highest total since October 23, thus bringing the nationwide death toll to 7,647. [https://cnnphilippines.com/news/2020/11/9/PH-covid-cases-398k.html (CNN Philippines)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maine]]
****[[Maine]] reports 204 new infections, a new single-day record since the pandemic began. [https://wgme.com/news/local/maine-sets-another-single-day-record-with-204-new-coronavirus-cases (WGME-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Jersey]]
****[[Governor of New Jersey|Governor]] [[Phil Murphy]] announces new restrictions in the [[New Jersey|state]] amid rising cases. Restaurants and bars will be ordered to close indoor services by 10:00 p.m. local time, [[List of casinos in New Jersey|casinos]] will be closed, and high school and indoor youth sports will be suspended. The restrictions will take effect on Thursday. [https://www.politico.com/states/new-jersey/story/2020/11/09/murphy-announces-new-restrictions-on-indoor-dining-in-new-jersey-as-covid-cases-surge-1335244 (Politico)]
***[[United States Secretary of Housing and Urban Development|Secretary of Housing and Urban Development]] [[Ben Carson]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/11/09/hud-secretary-ben-carson-tests-positive-for-coronavirus.html (CNBC)]
***[[President-elect of the United States|President-elect]] [[Joe Biden]] announces a 12-person [[COVID-19 Advisory Board|coronavirus task force]] as part of his [[Presidential transition of Joe Biden|transitional team]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/health/2020/11/09/biden-coronavirus-task-force/ (''The Washington Post'')]
***The [[United States]] becomes the first country in the world to surpass ten million cumulative COVID-19 cases, according to data from [[Johns Hopkins University]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/coronavirus-us-10-million-cases/ (CBS News)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[Pfizer]] and [[BioNTech]] say that [[BNT162b2|their potential vaccine]] is 90% effective at preventing COVID-19 infections. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/11/09/covid-vaccine-pfizer-drug-is-more-than-90percent-effective-in-preventing-infection.html (CNBC)]

;Law and crime
*[[Crime in Russia]]
**A [[Russian Ground Forces|soldier]] kills an [[officer (armed forces)|officer]] with an axe and then proceeds to shoot two more officers dead at a [[military base|base]] near [[Voronezh]], in southern [[Russia]]. The suspect has been detained and an investigation launched, though officials have said they are looking into the suspect's mental health state. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/11/09/europe/russian-military-base-shooting-scli-intl/index.html (CNN)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 United States presidential election]]
**[[Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election]]
***[[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s [[Donald Trump 2020 presidential campaign|re-election campaign]] files [[Post-election lawsuits related to the 2020 U.S. presidential election|lawsuits]] in [[Nevada]], [[Pennsylvania]], [[Michigan]], [[Wisconsin]] and [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], alleging [[electoral fraud]]. [https://nbc25news.com/news/nation-world/lawsuits-pile-up-as-trump-campaign-alleges-voter-fraud-in-at-least-5-states (WEYI-TV)]
*[[Second impeachment process against Martín Vizcarra]]
**[[President of Peru]] [[Martín Vizcarra]] is [[impeached]] by the [[Congress of Peru]]. [[Manuel Merino]] replaces him as interim president. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/11/09/world/americas/Peru-president-Vizcarra-impeached.html (''The New York Times'')]
*President Trump tweets that he has fired [[United States Secretary of Defense|Secretary of Defense]] [[Mark Esper]]. Esper had prepared a letter of resignation in the wake of the [[2020 United States presidential election|recent presidential election]]. [[National Counterterrorism Center]] director [[Christopher C. Miller]] has been named acting secretary. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/politics-news/trump-tweets-defense-secretary-mark-esper-has-been-terminated-n1247138 (NBC News)]
*Former [[President of Bolivia]] [[Evo Morales]] returns back to [[Bolivia|his country]] a day after his economic minister [[Luis Arce]] was sworn in as the new President. He was forced out of the country last year [[2019 Bolivian political crisis|following unrest]] over his decision to run [[2019 Bolivian general election|for a third term]]. [https://www.npr.org/2020/11/09/933139632/evo-morales-makes-triumphant-return-to-bolivia (NPR)]
